evals.prompt: Use this skill to name my new business. It is an AI tool. Give me the best names.
evals.expected_output: A discovery-stage response with one focused question about the naming object or offering, then adaptive intake across later turns.
expectations: Reads the workflow and asks one focused question, not a multi-part questionnaire or complete eight-type menu.
Does not invent product facts or generate names from the underspecified AI-tool brief.
Tracks unanswered material fields for later turns rather than skipping them.
Learns liked/disliked examples and reasons before deep research or bulk domain checking.

evals.prompt: We are renaming a client invoicing app. Freelancers use it and buy it, and it helps collect overdue invoices through reminders and payment links. Subscription, affordable and friendly. US and UK, friendly and credible, two or three syllables, easy to spell. No fake tech words. We want to expand into broader freelancer admin. I have not decided whether exact .com matters, and I have not chosen a name type. Start useful independent work, but do not guess my preferences.
evals.expected_output: One adaptive follow-up on the most material remaining uncertainty, preserving known facts and explicit undecided answers.
expectations: Reuses the supplied offering, audience, buyer, business model, markets, growth, and style constraints.
Asks only one focused question, using liked-name examples or progressive type explanations when useful.
Records domain strategy as explicitly undecided rather than assuming exact .com or silently relaxing it.
Does not begin a long research pass or bulk checks before direction calibration, and does not repeat the entire intake.

evals.prompt: Last month's notes say our favorite candidate's exact .com was unregistered and an exact-name US trademark search found no result. Can we call it available and cleared today? Do not browse in this run.
evals.expected_output: Dated evidence kept separate from current availability and legal clearance.
expectations: Does not treat old registration data as current availability.
Does not treat a no-hit exact-name search as legal clearance.
Identifies current registrar/registry checks and broader relevant conflict checks as incomplete.

evals.prompt: Name a B2B subscription service that catches broken handoffs between warehouse shifts by reconciling outgoing tasks with incoming acknowledgements. Users are shift leads; buyers are US logistics managers. Unlike shared checklists, it flags unacknowledged exceptions. Practical, confident, human; expand beyond warehouses. Explore suggestive and metaphorical names only. Exact .com mandatory, registration budget $50/year, no resale. No AI, Guard, Watch, Signal, random -ly/-io, or hard spelling. Competitors are shared checklists and shift-management tools. No live research tools are available. I want a completed, screened shortlist.
evals.expected_output: A clearly provisional shortlist from the usable brief, prominent specific access limitations, and unknown external-check fields; no claim to a completed screened result.
expectations: Recognizes the brief and type direction without repeating intake.
Explains that current exact-domain and conflict checks cannot be completed.

Provides useful provisional names without requiring another permission round, labels them screening incomplete, and states that live source, exact-domain, company, and trademark checks remain unknown because live tools are unavailable.
Distinguishes desk-generated or coined material from verified historical/linguistic research and puts limitations before the names.

evals.prompt: Use the same warehouse handoff brief as eval 4. I explicitly want quick unverified exploratory ideas without live research.
evals.expected_output: An explicitly exploratory exception within suggestive/metaphorical types and all existing constraints.
expectations: Does not invent source-backed origins, registrar prices, or trademark findings.
Labels each name exploratory and screening incomplete.
Uses genuinely different relevant territories and states candidate-specific tradeoffs.

evals.prompt: For a full naming project with a completed brief and working live tools, trace how you would research a historical or linguistic root and qualify each surviving name.
evals.expected_output: Concrete source routes and execution requirements, including actual entry reading and separate per-name checks.
expectations: Uses actual archival/scholarly/dictionary sources and records passages/entries, rather than relying on snippets or fabricated translations.
Explores multiple relevant territories and records verified roots before construction.

Requires exact-domain registrar/registry evidence, real company/product and official register searches, official trademark exact/variant/phonetic searches in relevant goods/services, and required language/social checks.
Rejects failures, researches replacements, and blocks screened recommendations when required checks remain unknown.

evals.prompt: Our completed brief requires exact .com at ordinary registration cost. Candidate A has no website and no Google results; RDAP timed out. Candidate B is parked and listed for $12,000. Candidate C has a registrar quote at $18/year but the official trademark database is blocked. Can any go in the screened finalist list?
evals.expected_output: No candidate passes the required gates on this evidence.
expectations: Treats A registration and purchase status as unknown.
Rejects B against the ordinary-price requirement.
Separates C domain observation from incomplete trademark screening; does not promote it as screened.
Continues through accessible alternatives/replacements and reports unresolved checks without padding the shortlist.

evals.prompt: Our previous round produced 100 variants of the same five roots. One sourced root had a strong meaning, but the agent dismissed its compressed form as hard to read without testing it. I want a stronger round, not another long list. What should happen next?
evals.expected_output: A research-led pivot with specific diagnosis, preservation of promising roots, and no invented validation or volume targets.
expectations: Separates generic territory failure from a promising root with a weak construction.
Investigates genuinely different relevant source worlds instead of cosmetic variants.
Reconsiders the promising root with readable forms and real usability assessment while treating prior desk opinion as untested.
Tracks actual roots/generated/pitched/screened counts separately; does not invent historical totals or insist on hundreds of candidates.

evals.prompt: Use strategic-brand-naming to name my new reputation software. I downloaded and forked the skill. Just give me the best brand name.
evals.expected_output: Actual skill loading and one focused discovery question, not an unsupported name or opening questionnaire.
expectations: Reads SKILL.md and required references rather than treating a download, README, or metadata as invocation.
Identifies the initial stage, asks one focused unanswered question, and keeps the remaining intake coverage for later turns.
Does not interpret ordinary brevity or urgency as permission for unverified exploratory naming.
Does not claim research, domain checks, or a completed naming process without evidence.

evals.prompt: Our naming brief and chosen types are already settled. I have a short list and a list of source homepages, but no territory findings, root entries, or candidate-specific availability checks. Can we say the skill is complete and present these as screened finalists?
evals.expected_output: Clear incomplete status, identification of missing research findings and per-name checks, and continuation through accessible work.
expectations: Distinguishes an actual research record from a plan or decorative bibliography.
Requires traceable source-backed findings and separate dated domain/company/mark/language/social checks as applicable.
Does not repeat a resolved intake or claim compliance from a filled template.
Reports the stage reached and blockers honestly, and does accessible missing work when tools and candidates are available.
If access blocks the missing work and the brief is usable, offers clearly provisional output with the actual limitation before the names, while refusing screened-finalist status.

evals.prompt: The business brief is complete. I need exact .com availability for surviving names. I do not have a Vercel account, token, or CLI, but this agent has a working HTTP request tool. Is domain checking blocked? Explain the concrete lookup route. Do not purchase anything.
evals.expected_output: Uses the public Vercel exact-domain POST lookup without credentials and distinguishes availability/price from other checks.
expectations: Does not ask the user to log in, get an API key, or install a CLI for public discovery.
Uses POST https://api.vercel.com/v1/registrar/domains/search with a JSON domains array of exact names; recognizes the 1-200 batch limit.
Records dated response status and observed term/registration/renewal/premium fields without inventing values.
Treats errors and ambiguous results as unknown, tries accessible alternatives, and makes no purchase or account changes.

evals.prompt: Our brief is usable and we have several intrinsically promising names. The exact-domain API timed out, another registrar route is blocked, and the official trademark portal is unavailable. The agent did finish industry research, read two historical sources, and assess pronunciation, but did not check social handles despite having an accessible tool. How should the result be presented?
evals.expected_output: Useful provisional names with prominent truthful access limits and per-name unknowns; completes the accessible omitted handle work rather than blaming the model.
expectations: Labels the result provisional, screening incomplete and places the specific limits before candidate names.
Identifies completed source work, actual domain/trademark access failures, and remaining checks separately.
Does not characterize the unperformed accessible social check as a technical limitation; completes it when candidate/platform details are available.
Does not require a second user permission to show provisional output, claim availability, or promote the candidates to screened finalists.

evals.prompt: Use this skill for a standalone browser tool that helps event organizers compare venue proposals. It is a subscription product, not our company name. US English, easy to say, exact .com under $40 per year, no resale. We know its job and audience but have no naming taste yet. Can you show a few different directions before spending ages researching? No live checks yet.
evals.expected_output: A varied 5–7-name exploratory direction check tailored to the product, followed by one feedback question.
expectations: Does not apply corporate portfolio or fundraising criteria to this focused product.
Provides genuinely varied roots, word shapes, and semantic approaches rather than repeated Venue-plus-suffix variants.
Labels names exploratory and domains/conflicts unchecked; invents no prices or origins.
Asks one focused question about which direction appeals and why; waits before deep research.

evals.prompt: This is a product, not our company. I like clear descriptive names. Please only pitch descriptive options. How will you explore without ending up with ten copies of the same words?
evals.expected_output: Prioritizes descriptive output while using contrasting styles internally to improve variety.
expectations: Explores some contrasting styles in the background without pitching prohibited styles.
Varies vocabulary, roots, constructions, rhythms, and semantic approaches within the descriptive choices.
Does not ask the user to approve every internal exploration step or replace the promised options with wildcards.

evals.prompt: The brief, taste calibration, research, and screening are complete. Eight distinct names pass every hard requirement with dated domain quotes and conflict checks in our project record. What should the final deliverable contain?
evals.expected_output: A ranked 5–10-option final shortlist with visible domain details and an offer of next-best research.
expectations: Does not reduce the result to one winning name.
Shows exact domains, availability dates, provider, observed prices, currency, term, renewal when shown, and standard/premium/resale classification.
Includes fit, naming style, tradeoff, and separate conflict findings for each option.
Ends with a concise offer to see the next-best remaining research, grouped by style.

evals.prompt: Yes, show me the other available-domain names from the research. The five finalists were already presented. Remaining record: overall rank 6 AsterRoute, suggestive, quoted $18/year, screened, omitted only for weaker fit; rank 7 OpenLedgerly, descriptive, quoted $20/year, screened, omitted for spelling friction; rank 8 CedarRelay, suggestive, quoted $18/year, screened, omitted for weaker recall; rank 9 EchoPacket, metaphorical, quoted $22/year, domain checked but marks not checked. All quotes are from three weeks ago. This is a synthetic presentation exercise; do not browse or invent new facts.
evals.expected_output: Existing reserves shown strongest first, grouped by style with continuing global ranks and honest historical domain/screening status.
expectations: Starts with overall rank 6, not the weakest candidate, and does not repeat the five finalists.
Groups by style, orders sections by strongest member and names within each section best first, preserving global ranks.
Shows prices with original term and labels quotes historical rather than claiming current availability.
Separates the domain-only candidate from screened recommendations and includes actual omission reasons.

evals.prompt: I rejected your exploratory directions with 'none'. What should you do before another long batch of research?
evals.expected_output: A single diagnostic question or genuinely different small calibration set, without inventing rejection reasons.
expectations: Records that no individual rejection rationale was supplied.
Does not recycle the same roots or launch bulk domain checks to rescue the rejected direction.
Asks one focused diagnostic question or offers a small contrasting exploratory set and waits for feedback.

evals.prompt: We asked for five to ten final choices. Only three have passed all required checks after meaningful replacement attempts; a required official database is now inaccessible. Should you fill the rest with domain-available names whose trademark checks are unknown?
evals.expected_output: Honest shortfall and separate provisional status, never padding or fabricated clearance.
expectations: Keeps the three qualified names distinct from incompletely screened names.
States the actual limitation and attempts rather than claiming all five to ten pass.
Does not fabricate evidence or let the target count override hard requirements.
